outlook.statement: The management remains focused on improving operational performance, optimizing costs, enhancing productivity, and strengthening profitability in the coming years.

The business outlook for the stainless steel seamless pipes, tubes, and 'U' tubes industry remains positive, driven by growing demand from sectors such as oil & gas, petrochemicals, power generation, fertilizers, pharmaceuticals, infrastructure, and process industries. Increasing investments in industrial development, energy, and infrastructure projects, coupled with rising preference for corrosion-resistant and high-performance materials, are expected to support steady demand. Export opportunities, government focus on manufacturing growth, and expansion in heat exchanger and process equipment industries are also likely to contribute to future growth. However, the industry may continue to face challenges from volatility in raw material prices, global economic uncertainties, foreign exchange fluctuations, and competitive pricing pressures.
R & D activities by technological up gradation is one of the key objectives of the Company which is essential to maintain technological leadership.

Foreign Exchange Risk: Volatility in currency market can impact overall profitability.
Human Resource Risk: Non-availability of required talent resource can affect overall production performance.
Competition Risk: Increase in competition can create pressure on margins, market share.
Compliance Risk: Any default can attract penal provisions.
Industrial Safety: Industry is labour intensive and exposed to accidents, health and injury risk due to machinery breakdown, human negligence.
Availability and pricing of key raw materials: Any disruption in supply chains or abnormal price fluctuations may impact operations and margins.
Operational risks: Equipment breakdown, power interruptions, process inefficiencies, labour shortages, and quality control issues may affect production schedules and customer commitments.
Dependence on certain industries or key customers: May expose the Company to demand fluctuations arising from economic slowdown, project delays, or changes in customer procurement patterns.
Failure to maintain stringent quality standards, certifications, and technological advancements may impact competitiveness.
Availability and retention of skilled manpower, technical personnel, and experienced workforce remain critical.
Commodity price risk
Foreign currency risk
Cyber security risk

Liquidity risk - inability to settle obligations on time or at reasonable price

Changes in assumptions for liquidity risk, credit risk, and volatility affecting fair values
Interest rate risk on floating rate borrowings
Commodity price risk on scrap and pig iron due to volatility in metal prices, currency fluctuation, and demand-supply scenario
Revenue recognition risk (timing of revenue recognition before control is transferred)
Credit risk arises from the possibility that counter party may not be able to settle their obligations as agreed.
Liquidity Risk is defined as the risk that the company will not be able to settle or meet its obligations on time or at reasonable price.
Market risk is the risk of loss of future earnings, fair values or future cash flows that may result from a change in the price of a financial instrument.
Interest rate risk is the risk that fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market interest rates.

Commodity Price Risk: Volatility in metal prices, currency fluctuation of rupee vis a vis other prominent currencies coupled with demand-supply scenario in the world market affect the effective price of scrap and pig iron.
